field_errors.evidence: the assumption of doping Li+ cations into A-site and Ta5+ and Nb5+ cations into the B-site of the cubic perovskite Sr(4B)O3 framework

verdicts.explanation: The 0.094 mS/cm LSTZ baseline is reported in Figure 1 as a comparison value measured in this work at 25 °C, so the value, material and origin hold. Sr is the host A-site cation of the SrZrO3-type framework, not a dopant, so listing it as a dopant is wrong.

The 0.218 mS/cm value for LSTNZS (y = 9/16) is labelled as total conductivity in the Figure 1 caption but as bulk conductivity (σbulk) in the main text and in the simulation comparison, so conductivity_kind 'total' conflicts with the paper's own body text and the kind cannot be confirmed.

The Figure 1 caption states that the Sn-free LSTNZH (grey circle, furnace-cooled) has a total ionic conductivity of 0.151 mS/cm, measured at 25 °C per the Electrical Measurements section, with 1300 °C / 12 h sintering.
The Figure 1 caption gives 0.256 mS/cm total conductivity for the quenched LSTNZH (red circle), and Figure 6 and the text confirm this is the air-quenched sample measured at 25 °C.
The paper reports σtotal = 1.47 × 10^-4 S/cm for air-quenched LSTNZS (y = 9/16), with conductivities measured at 25 °C and the sample described as experimental in this work.

The paper states that the MTP molecular dynamics simulation of LSTNZS (y = 9/16) gives a bulk ionic conductivity of 0.285 mS/cm at 300 K, which is a computed value from this paper, so the computational origin, the kind and the temperature conversion are correct.
